## Overview

Your second class project is an interpretive trail sign designed for one of the field sites we visit in class. This can be an expansion on your field guide, or you can use this opportunity to learn about a new ecosystem or site.

Prior to completing this planning assignment, read the final directions for the interpretive sign and review the examples.

## Assignment

In 1-3 sentences each, outline your ideas for the following:

### Basic information

- the field site on which you want to focus
- the dominant ecosystem at that site (hint: check the site presentations sheet)
- historical human interaction with the site or ecosystem
- current human interaction with the site or ecosystem

### Species of interest

For each of these components, describe _why_ they are relevant to the site _and_ ecosystem. Note that you may write more than 3 sentences for these components if needed.

- 2-3 primary producers 
- 2-3 consumers
- 2-3 predators

### Visual representations

Note that you may write more than 3 sentences for these components if needed.

Describe:

- how you want to visually represent the "wide view" of the ecosystem (examples include but are not limited to: map, landscape, cross-section), and why
- how you plan to visually represent species of interest and their interactions with each other and the environment

### Outline

Lastly, draw a potential layout for your interpretive sign. Use stick figures or coarse sketches for visual components, and shapes representing placeholders for each written section (including the title).
